rejectionReason: Author rejected the schematic illustrated treatment and oversized settlement scale; requested the built-in generator and the established Glowhaven rendering instead.
providerPrompt: Create ONE extraordinary, coherent, full-color illustrated fantasy WORLD MAP of a large inland Japanese-inspired Oni nation, a continuous rectangular country viewed from a very high oblique aerial cartographic perspective. Landscape 4:3. A beautiful finished game atlas with densely detailed miniature buildings, crisp drawn edges and luminous painterly 2D terrain, jewel-toned rivers, rich vegetation, warm early-autumn sunlight, precise miniature roofs and graceful mountains. Broad inhabited landscape at national scale, NOT a close view of one city. Show the entire land continuously all the way to the edges. Minimal atmospheric obstruction so terrain and landmarks remain readable. No writing, labels, numbers, markers, icons, drawn grid, legend, frame, coastline, ocean, floating islands, or separate panels. GEOGRAPHY: north is the top. A broad band of dense living forest encloses ALL FOUR outer margins; mountain forest also continues along the northern margin. It is land beyond the edge, never a coastline or island. Three distinct settlement centers amid vast countryside: ONE large capital in the center-right at about 63% across, 51% down; ONE much smaller western castle town at 14% across, 50% down; ONE much smaller eastern castle town at 87% across, 49% down. Capital is substantially larger than either town, yet most of the composition is wilderness and farms. The cities must fit comfortably inside their districts with generous intervening countryside. Scattered very small rural villages, shrine roofs and post towns complement them; do not duplicate capitals. HERO LANDMARK: a great sacred mountain rises in the north-center-right, around 63% across, 17% down, directly behind and above the capital. Steep forested lower slopes, pale exposed upper rock, a little high snow, a tiny summit shrine, cedar pilgrimage stairways, and a long white waterfall into the capital basin. At the accessible southern foot stands the capital's magnificent but believable terraced Shogunal castle: layered ivory-and-dark-timber Japanese roofs, stone retaining walls, elegant watchtowers, gardens and stairs. The capital spreads southward below it into compact market wards, canals, workshops, homes, a great river bridge, martial courtyards, and a controlled transit-shrine compound with one visible vermilion torii. A distinctive timber guild hall near a bridge and market. Keep the castle/capital complex clearly separate from the summit shrine. A second much older, smaller torii is hidden in a cedar grove on the mountain's lower flank, away from the capital transit compound, with no glowing portal vortex. NORTHWEST: dark pine woodland, broken watchtower ruin, a dramatic narrow ravine crossed by one little bridge and a tiny resin-cutters' hamlet. NORTH MID-LEFT: rugged gray Thundercrag ridges, a terraced working quarry with a winding haul road, small mountain forge roofs, cascading stream and a guarded pass. NORTHEAST: a high snowcedar pass, distant snow-streaked peaks, cold forest, a small frozen mountain tarn and a warm-roofed roadside lodge. Snow follows elevation naturally, without square biome borders. MIDDLE WEST: the small western castle town is a practical river fortress with a modest keep, low walls, boats and a recognizable twin-arch bridge. MIDDLE MID-LEFT: lush tall emerald bamboo valleys, a winding lantern road, a gorge with flowing water, a tiny bamboo-craft village and a secluded roof compound.
